answer: Since the forge verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the tundra audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, as the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own ocean path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 25 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 2 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
